assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology through to GLP-1-based therapies is a rare complete arc from hormone biology to a transformative treatment for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large, clear and lasting clinical and physiological impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 biology and secretion in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 action, proglucagon processing, GLP-2) and Mojsov (peptide chemistry and identification of the active GLP-1 form) are the strongest basic-science trio from the supplied names. Knudsen (industrial development of liraglutide/semaglutide) and others, and Habener's role outside this list, leave the allocation contested.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation is exceptionally strong through large independent randomized outcome trials and widespread clinical use; recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit among Mojsov, Habener-group work and others is disputed and the list does not include every plausible contributor.
Whether the prize should centre on basic physiology or on drug development is unresolved.
I have not independently verified the details of the credit dispute.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering a patient's T cells to recognise cancer produced durable remissions in refractory leukemias and lymphomas, a clear conceptual and clinical breakthrough with large impact on cancer immunotherapy.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (CD28-costimulated CARs, preclinical proof) and June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL, 4-1BB constructs) are central; Rosenberg's adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T-cell trials supply foundational clinical proof. Eshhar and others, who made the first CARs, are not among the supplied names, which weakens fairness of any configuration.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products, multi-year follow-up and independent confirmation show a mature field, though the solid-tumor setting remains unsolved.
uncertainties: Absence of first-generation CAR inventors in the credited names complicates attribution.
Long-term safety, relapse and limits in solid tumors persist.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology causal, cell-type-specific control with light, transforming experimental design across fields; the originality and breadth of impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin characterisation) and Deisseroth (neuronal implementation and broad toolkit) form a coherent trio; Boyden, Bamberg and Miesenböck have legitimate claims, so exclusions are contentious.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for two decades; clinical use is limited but the tool's maturity is not in doubt.
uncertainties: Several credible claimants must be excluded under the three-person limit.
The value is mainly methodological rather than a disease-directed discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 identified a distinct class of oncogene that blocks cell death, founding the control of apoptosis in cancer and enabling BH3-mimetic therapy such as venetoclax; the discovery is original and clinically validated.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams led the Walter and Eliza Hall work on BCL-2 and its regulation; Vaux showed BCL-2 cooperates with myc and promotes survival. Strasser's contributions are significant but later. Foundational credit also involves Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer, who are not in the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by independent work, apoptosis was previously recognised in 2002, and venetoclax is now an established therapy, so timing is favorable.
uncertainties: The 2002 prize for apoptosis genetics may be seen as overlapping.
Excluded early BCL-2 cloners and the deceased Korsmeyer complicate fairness.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway explains how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, linking infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and anti-tumour immunity; it is conceptually clear and broadly influential.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and cGAMP identification) and Barber (STING discovery) are the decisive contributors from the supplied list; Ishikawa, Sun and Wu contributed but are more junior or overlapping.
assessment.maturity: The mechanism is robustly confirmed, though therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) is still unproven clinically, so timing is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical benefit of pathway modulation is not yet established.
Credit division between STING and cGAS discovery groups and the roles of Ishikawa, Sun and Wu need adjudication.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed ER-to-nucleus signalling that governs proteostasis, with relevance to diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer; it is elegant, original and widely taught.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori independently defined the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 signalling pathway, which makes a two-person configuration natural; Kevin Lee and others contributed less decisively. This pair has a clean claim.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation; the biology is stable, though direct therapeutic payoff remains modest.
uncertainties: Translational impact is less direct than for other candidates.
Roles of other pathway discoverers (e.g. PERK, ATF6) are not credited in this list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Adult stem-cell-derived organoids opened a general platform for modelling tissue biology and disease and began to affect drug testing and personalised medicine; the Lgr5 stem-cell work underpinning it is original and widely adopted.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid culture work, with Sato the first author of the founding gut organoid paper; the pair is a plausible fair configuration, but wider contributions (e.g. Wnt biology, Sasai's ES-derived organoids) are outside the credited names.
assessment.maturity: Very widely reproduced; clinical impact is still emerging, so the prize may be seen as slightly early or as best framed around stem-cell biology.
uncertainties: Whether the discovery is a method or a conceptual advance is open.
Competing organoid lineages are not represented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense modulation of SMN2 splicing led to nusinersen, converting spinal muscular atrophy from a fatal childhood disease into a treatable one; the mechanistic clarity and clinical effect are striking.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (splicing mechanism and ISS-N1 target discovery) and Bennett (antisense chemistry and drug development) are the key credited contributors; a two-person prize seems coherent, though other contributors to the SMN2 targeting insight are not listed.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with robust long-term and independent confirmation; recognition is timely and may be seen as an RNA-therapeutics prize.
uncertainties: The relative weight of academic mechanism versus industrial drug development is debatable.
Other contributors to the ISS-N1 and antisense work may need recognition.
